chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures a person's planned entry to an event venue.

candidates.label: ticketToken
candidates.comment: A textual or URL reference to an asset, such as a barcode or QR code, that can be used for entrance with a ticket. Also called "entrance token", "access code", "QR code link", "barcode reference". Examples: "The ticket has ticketToken a QR code image URL", "The event ticket's ticketToken is a barcode string", "This ticket provides a ticketToken for entry."

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: tocEntry
candidates.comment: A table of contents entry relation between a HyperToc and one of its constituent HyperToc entries. Also called contains entry, includes entry, part of toc. Examples: "HyperToc tocEntry 'Introduction'", "HyperToc tocEntry 'Section 1.1'", "HyperToc tocEntry 'Conclusion'".

candidates.label: uses
candidates.comment: Indicates an entity employing another entity for a specific purpose.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: usedIn
candidates.comment: Indicates the context or location where something is utilized or prevalent.

candidates.label: arrivalPlatform
candidates.comment: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."

candidates.label: ticketedSeat
candidates.comment: An association between a ticket and the specific seat it grants access to. Also called "assigned seat", "seat number", "ticket seat allocation". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketedSeat Row A, Seat 12", "The flight ticket's ticketedSeat is 23F", "This ticket is for a specific ticketedSeat."

relations.embedding_query_text: is themed after:

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org property 'subjectOf' is the best fit for a product being thematically related to a state.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: isDecorationOf
candidates.comment: Indicates the item that serves as a decoration.

candidates.label: occursAfter
candidates.comment: Indicates that the subject event occurs chronologically after the object event.

candidates.label: postOp
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing the postoperative procedures, care, or follow-ups associated with a medical device. Also called aftercare, post-surgery instructions, recovery protocol. Examples: A medical device has post-op instructions for 'wound care'. The implant has post-op guidelines for 'activity restrictions'. The procedure involves post-op follow-ups for 'device monitoring'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: followup
candidates.comment: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".

candidates.label: isPreviousFilmInSeries
candidates.comment: The subject movie is the preceding film in the specified franchise.

candidates.label: containsSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

relations.embedding_query_text: is in honor of:

chosen_property.label: inHonorOf
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a product or item is dedicated to or celebrates a person.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures the 'in honor of' relationship for a product and a person.

candidates.label: honorificSuffix
candidates.comment: An honorific suffix relation between a person and a title following their name. Also called post-nominal title, suffix title, academic suffix. Examples: "A person has an honorific suffix 'PhD'.", "His honorific suffix is 'M.D.'.", "The individual uses the honorific suffix 'Jr.'."

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: isDecorationOf
candidates.comment: Indicates the item that serves as a decoration.

candidates.label: isFamilyMemberOf
candidates.comment: Indicates the person or group to whom a family member role belongs.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: forPurpose
candidates.comment: Indicates the intended goal or reason for an action or entity.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: awardsGiven
candidates.comment: Indicates the specific award or title conferred during an award ceremony.

candidates.label: personInvolved
candidates.comment: Indicates a person associated with an event or duration.

relations.embedding_query_text: is student of:

chosen_property.label: studies
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the field of study or specialty a person is a student of.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly links a person to their field of study or cultural interest.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: educationalRole
candidates.comment: An educational role relation between an educational audience and the text describing its specific role. Also called "audience role", "learner role", "student type". Examples: "Educational audience educationalRole 'Student'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Teacher'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Parent'".

candidates.label: maximumEnrollment
candidates.comment: An enrollment capacity relation between an educational or occupational program and the maximum number of students who can be enrolled. Also called: enrollment limit, student capacity, maximum participants. Examples: "Master's Program maximumEnrollment 50", "Workshop maximumEnrollment 20", "Online Course maximumEnrollment 500".

candidates.label: financialAidEligible
candidates.comment: A financial aid eligibility relation between a course or educational program and the types of financial aid students can use to cover its costs. Also called: aid programs, funding options, scholarship eligibility. Examples: "Computer Science Course" financial aid eligible "Federal Pell Grant", "MBA Program" financial aid eligible "Student Loans", "Vocational Training" financial aid eligible "GI Bill".

candidates.label: totalHistoricalEnrollment
candidates.comment: A total historical enrollment relation between a course and the cumulative number of students who have ever enrolled in it. Also called cumulative enrollment, past enrollment count, historical student count. Examples: "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '500'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '1200'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '75'".

candidates.label: typicalCreditsPerTerm
candidates.comment: A typical credits per term relation between an educational or occupational program and the expected number of credits a full-time student would take in one term. Also called term credits, unit load per term, average credits. Examples: "EducationalOccupationalProgram typicalCreditsPerTerm '15'", "Program typicalCreditsPerTerm '12 units'", "WorkBasedProgram typicalCreditsPerTerm '9'".

candidates.label: educationalLevel
candidates.comment: An educational level relation between a creative work, event, credential, or resource and its progression level in an educational context. Also called "learning level", "proficiency level", "grade level". Examples: "Textbook educationalLevel 'Intermediate'", "Course 'Calculus I' educationalLevel 'University Level'", "Credential 'High School Diploma' educationalLevel 'Secondary Education'".

candidates.label: instructor
candidates.comment: An instructional role relation between a course instance and the person who teaches or assists in teaching it. Also called teacher, lecturer, tutor, educator, faculty. Examples: A calculus course instance has 'Dr. Smith' as its instructor. A yoga class has 'Jane Doe' as its instructor. A coding bootcamp lists 'John Johnson' as an instructor.

candidates.label: teaches
candidates.comment: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."

relations.embedding_query_text: has characteristic:

chosen_property.label: hasCharacteristic
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a characteristic or attribute of an entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures a general 'has characteristic' relationship for an event venue and an age descriptor.

candidates.label: characteristicOf
candidates.comment: Indicates a characteristic or attribute of an entity.

candidates.label: hasAppearanceOf
candidates.comment: Describes a perceived characteristic or legitimacy associated with the subject.

candidates.label: amenityFeature
candidates.comment: An amenity feature relation between an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place and a characteristic or service it offers. Also called facility, service, characteristic, convenience. Examples: "A hotel room's amenity feature is 'free Wi-Fi'.", "The apartment's amenity feature is 'gym access'.", "A park's amenity feature is 'playground'."

candidates.label: pertainsToProperty
candidates.comment: Indicates the property or characteristic that a subject pertains to or defines.

candidates.label: characterAttribute
candidates.comment: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".

candidates.label: hasSpecialty
candidates.comment: Indicates a specific area of expertise or professional focus for a person.

candidates.label: identifiesMarker
candidates.comment: Points out a specific ingredient or characteristic that serves as an indicator, as part of guidance.

candidates.label: hasMemberType
candidates.comment: Describes the constituent types of members that form an alliance or coalition.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: Indicates the occupation of a person or group identified by a family role.

candidates.label: populationDescription
candidates.comment: Describes the population characteristics of a town.
